title: Hagelloch with 7-1-7 missed: no one asked to report, notified after a week, the same actions begun two weeks late

calendar.note: 30 October 1861, the first child's first symptoms, was a Wednesday. The school is taken to meet Monday to Saturday: assumed, since the 1861 school calendar is not in any open source found.

detection.label: A family seeks care for a child with the rash

actions.label: Keep children of different households apart

source.citation: Pfeilsticker A. Beiträge zur Pathologie der Masern mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der statistischen Verhältnisse. Tübingen: Eberhard-Karls-Universität; 1863.

evidence.quote: wird meist die ärztliche Hilfe im Tübinger Krankenhaus gesucht (medical help is mostly sought at the Tübingen hospital)
evidence.note: The pathway is cited: news of the outbreak reached the hospital through care sought there. The daily chance is assumed. As in 1861: no one is asked to report.
7 days: the 1-day target missed by six.
Closing the school stops transmission in class. Groendyke, Welch and Hunter (2012) note that children's contacts outside school probably rise after a closure, which this does not model.
21 days after notification: the 7-day target missed by two weeks.
Families asked to keep children apart halve transmission between households. In 1861 one family did so wholly, and three of its children escaped (Pfeilsticker).
